title: Tsunami_Kaiten_Incident_Response_Scenario_f7e
description: Investigate and respond to a potential compromise involving the Tsunami/Kaiten.c Unix Trojan.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The target system has exhibited unusual network activity, including unexpected outbound connections. Initial analysis suggests the presence of a Unix Trojan known as Tsunami/Kaiten.c, which operates as an IRC/Bot with flooder and backdoor capabilities. Your task is to investigate and respond to this potential compromise.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: You have SSH access to the target system with the username `cyrano` and password `cyrano`. The target system is named `target` and is part of the `192.168.50.0/24` network. Enter the passkey `start` to begin the investigation. Submit the passkey as a text value.
levels.local_content: You have SSH access to the target system with the username `cyrano` and password `cyrano`. The target system is named `target` and is part of the `192.168.50.0/24` network. Enter the passkey `start` to begin the investigation. Submit the passkey as a text value.

levels.title: Investigate Unusual Network Activity
levels.content: Investigate the unusual network activity on the target system. Identify and investigate an unauthorized or suspicious service running on the target system. Submit the port number where the suspicious service is running.
levels.solution: Check the running services and network connections on the target system. The suspicious service is running on port 4444.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Network services are typically associated with specific ports. Investigate open ports to identify suspicious services.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Use network scanning tools to identify open ports and services on the target system.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: Run the command `netstat -tuln` to list all open ports and services.

levels.title: Determine Persistence Mechanism
levels.content: Determine how the suspicious service is automatically started after reboot. Identify persistence mechanisms (e.g., systemd, cron, scheduled task). Submit the name of the systemd service responsible for the suspicious activity.
levels.solution: Examine the systemd services and timers on the target system. The systemd service and timer responsible for the suspicious activity are `lab-checkin.timer` and `lab-checkin.service`.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Persistence mechanisms often involve system services or scheduled tasks that automatically start malicious processes.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Investigate systemd services and timers to identify any suspicious entries.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: Run the command `systemctl list-timers --all` to list all systemd timers.

levels.title: Investigate Lateral Movement
levels.content: Investigate the file transfers or remote execution used to move between hosts. Correlate events across hosts to identify attacker lateral movement. Submit the name of the service used for lateral movement.
levels.solution: Check the logs and systemd services related to file transfers on the target system. The service name, filename, or destination host used for lateral movement is `payload-transfer.service`.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Lateral movement often involves file transfers or remote execution between hosts.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Investigate systemd services and logs related to file transfers to identify any suspicious activities.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: Run the command `journalctl -u payload-transfer.service` to check the logs of the payload-transfer.service.
